knowledge:
- key_parameters: nucleus=Specifies the marker channel to use as a nuclei marker for segmentation (e.g., "HH3") ;; transform=Specifies simple image transformations (e.g., "sqrt") to apply before segmentation ;; watershed=Specifies the watershedding method ("distance", "intensity", or "combine") ;; cellBody=Specifies the cell body identification method ("dilation", "discModel", "marker", or "None") ;; discSize=Specifies the size of the dilation in pixels when cellBody is "dilation" ;; cores=Specifies the number of cores to use for parallel processing ;; assayIn=The input assay name in the SingleCellExperiment object containing raw counts (e.g., "counts") ;; assayOut=The output assay name for normalized values (e.g., "norm") ;; transformation=Transformation method to apply during normalization (e.g., "sqrt") ;; method=Normalization method(s) to apply (e.g., "mean", "minMax", "trim99", "PC1")
- alternatives: EBImage=Recommended for users who need more flexibility when performing segmentation in R ;; External segmentation programs=simpleSeg is preferred when users want to perform the entire segmentation and extraction pipeline directly in R without external tools
- when_to_use: When analyzing multiplexed cellular imaging data (e.g., MIBI-TOF, IMC) stored as TIFF stacks and wanting to perform nuclei/cell segmentation, feature extraction, and marker normalization entirely within R.
- pitfalls: Marker intensities can be highly skewed (e.g., PanKRT), requiring careful selection of transformation and normalization methods (like trim99 and minMax) to achieve bimodal distributions suitable for clustering. Ensure the correct channel name is passed to the nucleus parameter.

workflows.name: multiplexed_image_segmentation_and_normalization
workflows.intent: Segment multiplexed images to identify cell boundaries, extract single-cell features, and normalize marker intensities.
workflows.stages: 1. Load multiplexed images from TIFF files and convert them to a CytoImageList ;; 2. Perform cell segmentation using a nuclear marker to generate segmentation masks ;; 3. Extract single-cell features (intensities and morphology) from the masks and images into a SingleCellExperiment ;; 4. Normalize and transform the extracted single-cell marker intensities
workflows.code:
pathToImages <- system.file("extdata", package = "simpleSeg")
imageDirs <- dir(pathToImages, "Point", full.names = TRUE)
names(imageDirs) <- dir(pathToImages, "Point", full.names = FALSE)
files <- files <- lapply(
  imageDirs,
  list.files,
  pattern = "tif",
  full.names = TRUE
)
images <- lapply(files, EBImage::readImage, as.is = TRUE)
images <- cytomapper::CytoImageList(images)
mcols(images)$imageID <- names(images)
masks <- simpleSeg::simpleSeg(images,
  nucleus = "HH3",
  transform = "sqrt"
)
cellSCE <- cytomapper::measureObjects(masks, images, img_id = "imageID")
cellSCE <- normalizeCells(cellSCE,
  assayIn = "counts",
  assayOut = "norm",
  imageID = "imageID",
  transformation = "sqrt",
  method = c("trim99", "minMax")
)
